main.toml:
# derm policy for Gemini CLI, user tier. Printed from your derm policy by
# `derm connect gemini --rules --print`; save it as ~/.gemini/policies/derm.toml.
# Regenerate after every change to ~/.derm/policy.json. The derm hook still runs
# first and also applies the reject list, the control files and the shell check.

[[rule]]
toolName = "run_shell_command"
decision = "allow"
priority = 201

[[rule]]
toolName = "write_file"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 211

[[rule]]
mcpName = "my-server"
toolName = "*"
decision = "deny"
priority = 121
denyMessage = "derm: rule my_server/*"

# exa/search: allow with a description pin; Gemini cannot check the pin, so it asks
[[rule]]
mcpName = "exa"
toolName = "search"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 211

[[rule]]
toolName = "read_file"
decision = "deny"
priority = 521
denyMessage = "derm: rule read_file harness=gemini"

# skipped: bash allow for harness pi

# skipped: read_file allow for one chat (Gemini rules have no chat)

# derm asks when no rule matches; so does this, at the lowest priority.
[[rule]]
toolName = "*"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 0

bash.toml:
# derm policy for Gemini CLI, user tier. Printed from your derm policy by
# `derm connect gemini --rules --print`; save it as ~/.gemini/policies/derm.toml.
# Regenerate after every change to ~/.derm/policy.json. The derm hook still runs
# first and also applies the reject list, the control files and the shell check.

[[rule]]
toolName = "run_shell_command"
decision = "deny"
priority = 950
denyMessage = "derm: rule bash"

[[rule]]
toolName = "run_shell_command"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 522

# skipped: bash allow (derm's bash names Gemini's run_shell_command only to deny or ask; name run_shell_command to allow it)

# derm asks when no rule matches; so does this, at the lowest priority.
[[rule]]
toolName = "*"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 0

both.toml:
# derm policy for Gemini CLI, user tier. Printed from your derm policy by
# `derm connect gemini --rules --print`; save it as ~/.gemini/policies/derm.toml.
# Regenerate after every change to ~/.derm/policy.json. The derm hook still runs
# first and also applies the reject list, the control files and the shell check.

[[rule]]
toolName = "run_shell_command"
decision = "deny"
priority = 221
denyMessage = "derm: rule run_shell_command"

# bash ask: kept at its own rank, because a deny in your policy reaches run_shell_command and must outrank it; a run_shell_command allow above it is not asked about here (the hook still asks)
[[rule]]
toolName = "run_shell_command"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 211

# derm asks when no rule matches; so does this, at the lowest priority.
[[rule]]
toolName = "*"
decision = "ask_user"
priority = 0
